newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman announces signing of $400 mln syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: Oman announces signing of $400 mln syndicated loan.

text.p: Oman on Wednesday said it had signed a $400 million, seven-year syndicated loan with local and international financial institutions to repay some of the country's debts and finance new projects.
A statement by Oman's ministry of economy said the agreement was signed with Bahrain-based Gulf International Bank and representatives of 36 other local and international financial institutions.
It did not name the other banks, but said they were 11 local and Arab banks, 13 European, two American and 10 Japanese banks.

"The loan will be used to repay some debts and to finance some projects not accounted for in the five-year plan like the ports of Raysut and Sohar," Economy Minister Ahmad bin Abdul-Nabi Mekki told reporters.
He said the new agreement would not affect the ceiling of government debt during the 1996-2000 plan which would remain at 1.5 billion rials ($3.94 billion). ($1=0.38 rials)
